* agent assistant

Agents can fulfill many tasks. The work has shifted from the paradigm of executing tasks (and often not document them) to document first what you want to do and plan (or let plan) the agents to execute.
The most important task is to test and quality check the results which means to own the pipeline and put enough logs and monitoring tools to allow traceability (know what agent did what).

We need an interface which is usually an IDE or a terminal to plan and orchestrate everything.

Here the choice is:

- IDE :: emacs because you focus on typing and don't get distracted by useless information
- format :: .org files: they contain agenda, trees, graphs, attributes, source code... you can basically write a complete software within a file
- LLM :: ollama because it's important to own the processes and limit spending
- coding agent :: currently on [[https://pi.dev/][pi-agent]], [[https://opencode.ai/][opencode]] and [[https://aider.chat/][aider]] where not efficient with local models. Aider UX is limited (no autocompletion, messed up my repo)
- MCP :: language models work at best with tools, I keep building MCP servers to ease LLM tasks
- graphs :: all the results are outputted in nodes and links to be visualized and navigated. I use [[https://neo4j.com/][neo4j]] to store the data
- programming :: mainly in python using REPL functionalities in emacs to test and execute every single line of code and check the data results
- deploy :: all the resources with docker so I can easily move them around
- hardware :: local: laptop and jetson

* models

Using mainly [[https://ollama.com/][ollama]] (with [[https://llama.app/][llama cpp]] took a lot of time for configuration) to serve LLMs.
Ollama has a nice interface for python which basically removed all my external dependencies from langchain and llamaindex (which keeps on changing APIs and packaging and my code needs to be re-written over and over).

- `qwen2.5-coder:3b` :: I use it a lot for summarization tasks, it's quick but sometimes output trivial content
- `qwen3.5:9b` :: The least thinking model I can use

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Convert .org files to single HTML slide per h1 section (*heading)."""
import re
from pathlib import Path
from html import escape
from urllib.parse import quote
from datetime import datetime

def process_heading(heading):
    """Process heading to remove cloaked content."""
    heading = ' '.join(heading).strip()
    heading = re.sub(r'\(file:.*?\)', '', heading)
    heading = re.sub(r'\[image:.*?\]', '', heading)
    heading = re.sub(r'\[link:.*?\]', '', heading)
    heading = re.sub(r'\[.+?\]\(', '', heading)
    heading = re.sub(r'\[.+?\]', '', heading)
    heading = re.sub(r'\{.*?\}', '', heading)
    heading = re.sub(r'#+name:\s*', '', heading)
    heading = re.sub(r':@TODO:', '', heading)
    heading = re.sub(r':@$TODO:', '', heading)
    heading = re.sub(r':@[^:]+:', '', heading)
    heading = heading.strip()
    return heading if heading else 'section'

def heading_to_slug(heading):
    """Convert heading to URL-safe slug."""
    slug = re.sub(r'[^\w\s\-]', '', heading).lower().strip()
    slug = re.sub(r'\s+', '-', slug)
    slug = re.sub(r'--+', '-', slug)
    slug = re.sub(r'[-_]+', '-', slug)
    slug = re.sub(r'[\(\)\[\]\:\;\{\}]+', '', slug)
    return slug if slug else 'section'

def clean_content(content):
    """Clean content lines for HTML."""
    lines = []
    for line in content:
        if not line.startswith('*'):
            continue
        if '#+begin_src' in line:
            continue
        if line.startswith('#+') or line.startswith(':'):
            continue
        if line.startswith('+#'):
            continue
        clean = line
        clean = re.sub(r'\(file:.*?\)', 'FILE', clean)
        clean = re.sub(r'\[image:.*?\]', '', clean)
        clean = re.sub(r'\[link:.*?\]', '', clean)
        clean = re.sub(r'\[.+?\]\(', '', clean)

''')
    return f'''

def main():
    import argparse
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Convert .org files to HTML slides')
    parser.add_argument('directory', help='Directory containing .org files')
    parser.add_argument('-o', '--output', help='Output directory')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    
    input_path = Path(args.directory).resolve()
    org_files = sorted([f for f in input_path.glob('*.org') if not f.name.startswith('.')], key=lambda x: x.name)
    
    if not org_files:
        print(f'No .org files found in {input_path}')
        return
    
    output_dir = Path(args.output).resolve() if args.output else input_path / 'html'
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    
    print(f'Converting .org files to HTML slides...')
    print(f'Input:  {input_path}')
    print(f'Output: {output_dir}')
    print(f'Found  {len(org_files)} .org files')
    print('=' * 60)
    
    total_slides = 0
    
    for org_file in org_files:
        print(f'\n📁 {org_file.name}')
        print('=' * 60)
        
        sections = parse_org_file(org_file)
        
        if not sections:
            print(f'  No sections found (only contains formatting)')
            continue
        
        title = 'Blender CV: ' + org_file.name.replace('.org', '')
        
        content_lines = []
        for sec_title, sec_content in enumerate(sections, 1):
            sec_title = sec_title if sec_title else f'Section {{sec}}.1'
            
            for line in sec_content:
                if line:
                    clean = re.sub(r'\(file:.*?\)', '', line)
                    clean = re.sub(r'\[.*?\]', '', clean)
                    clean = re.sub(r'#+', '', clean)
                    clean = re.sub(r':@', '', clean)
                    clean = clean.strip()
                    if clean:
                        content_lines.append(clean)
        
        if content_lines:
            content_html = ''.join(content_lines)
            html = generate_html(title, content_lines)
            
            file_slug = org_file.name.replace('.org', '')
            html_path = output_dir / (file_slug + '.html')
            
            with open(html_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                f.write(html)
            
            print(f'  Created: {html_path}')
            print(f'  Total:  {{total_slides}} slide(s)')
    
    print(f'\n' + '=' * 60)
    print(f'✓ Conversion complete!')
    print(f'Total slides: {{total_slides}}')
    print(f'Output: {{output_dir}}')
    print('\n  - index.html (list of all org files)')
    print(f'  - {{*}}.html (each org file with slides)')
    
    index_html = create_index(org_files)
    index_path = output_dir / 'index.html'
    with open(index_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write(index_html)
    
    return total_slides

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

content.text:
agent assistant

Agents can fulfill many tasks. The work has shifted from the paradigm of executing tasks (and often not document them) to document first what you want to do and plan (or let plan) the agents to execute. The most important task is to test and quality check the results which means to own the pipeline and put enough logs and monitoring tools to allow traceability (know what agent did what). We need an interface which is usually an IDE or a terminal to plan and orchestrate everything. Here the choice is: - IDE :: emacs because you focus on typing and don't get distracted by useless information - format :: .org files: they contain agenda, trees, graphs, attributes, source code... you can basically write a complete software within a file - LLM :: ollama because it's important to own the processes and limit spending - coding agent :: currently on [[https://pi.dev/][pi-agent]], [[https://opencode.ai/][opencode]] and [[https://aider.chat/][aider]] where not efficient with local models. Aider UX is limited (no autocompletion, messed up my repo) - MCP :: language models work at best with tools, I keep building MCP servers to ease LLM tasks - graphs :: all the results are outputted in nodes and links to be visualized and navigated. I use [[https://neo4j.com/][neo4j]] to store the data - programming :: mainly in python using REPL functionalities in emacs to test and execute every single line of code and check the data results - deploy :: all the resources with docker so I can easily move them around - hardware :: local: laptop and jetson Using mainly [[https://ollama.com/][ollama]] (with [[https://llama.app/][llama cpp]] took a lot of time for configuration) to serve LLMs. Ollama has a nice interface for python which basically removed all my external dependencies from langchain and llamaindex (which keeps on changing APIs and packaging and my code needs to be re-written over and over). I currently manage to run: - `qwen2.5-coder:3b` :: I use it a lot for summarization tasks, it's quick but sometimes output trivial content - `qwen3.5:9b` :: The least thinking model I can use - `qwen3.6:latest` :: At the hardware limits of my local setup, it is not worth it the waiting, really few tokens per second - `llama3.2:latest` :: - `codegemma:7b` :: - `deepseek-coder:6.7b` :: - `gemma4:latest` :: - `dolphin-mistral` :: The current coding assistant is on [[https://pi.dev/][pi-agent]] while [[https://opencode.ai/][opencode]], [[https://aider.chat/][aider]] and [[https://cursor.com/][cursor]] where also tested. - pi-agent :: currently the running options because it's more efficient for local models. It reduces the load and unload of files and the number of tokens. - cursor :: is not opensource and I can't integrated in my workflow. Cursor itself said that with using python REPL emacs it's the best option - aider :: I find it less invasive than opencode but struggles to perform simple operations and creates a lot of junk in the folder - opecode :: a bit too invasive for my taste, it takes too many autonomous decisions making it difficult to control Emacs integrates bash commands with macros and program outputs, I can connect language models with mcp servers. I currently use [[./emacs.el][emacs.el]] as current init file and [[./gptel_tools/el][gptel_tools.el]] for connecting with mcp. [[./gptell_allowed_commands.txt][gptel allowed commands]] is an additional list of bash commands which the tool allows Features: - LLMs :: I use different packages to interact with the local models - [[https://github.com/s-kostyaev/ellama][ellama]] :: for reasoning and structuring the project and for code examples in any buffer - [[https://github.com/karthink/gptel][gptel]] :: for the integration with mcp - [[https://github.com/lizqwerscott/mcp.el][mcp]] :: for adding my own tools and external mcp - [[https://github.com/MatthewZMD/aidermacs][aideremacs]] :: connect aider with emacs but was creating too much trash in the repository - [[https://github.com/dnouri/pi-coding-agent][pi agent]] :: connect pi-agent with emacs The [[https://orgmode.org/features.html][org mode]] is the most expressive way to structure projects or take notes. .org files allow a really expressive integration of information: - agenda :: to schedule a task or to set an alert [C-c a] - tags :: to specify meta information for that section [C-c C-q] - status :: whether an action is done or pending [Space - left/right arrow] - trees :: explain hierarchical structures [::] - code :: define code to execute `#+begin_src bash` `#+end_src` - graph :: interconnect elements - plots :: plot data with gnuplot - link :: link to anything: files, websites, buffers, images... - [[shell:ls *org][local org files]] :: open new buffers from shell A python Add gptel tools (defun my/read-buffer-content (buffer-name) (let ((buffer (get-buffer buffer-name))) (if (bufferp buffer) (with-current-buffer buffer (concat "[BUFFER CONTENT]: "(buffer_string))) "[ERROR]: Buffer does not exist"))) (defun my/llm-list-buffers () (apply 'concat (mapcar (lambda (buffer) (concat (buffer-name buffer) "\n")) (buffer-list)))) (gptel-make-tool (gptel-make-tool Display system information | Headline | Time | |--------------+--------| | *Total time* | *0:00* | Call internal endpoint curl -s -X PORT http://localhost:9876/run -H 'Content-Type: applicationon/json -d {"text":"Add a cube at origin and rotate it by 90 degrees z"}' List the file to edit ls -S ~/lav/siti/spiega/markdown | tail -n 5 Plot a graph | Sede | Max cites | H-index | |-----------+-----------+---------| | Chile | 257.72 | 21.39 | | Leeds | 165.77 | 19.68 | | Sao Paolo | 71.00 | 11.50 | | Stockholm | 134.19 | 14.33 | | Morelia | 257.56 | 17.67 | Find relevant files rg -l "auth|token" ./ echo "ciccia" $fileL aider $fileL --message "$instruction" echo $fileL I currently have the following mcp servers: - We need an interface which is usually an IDE or a terminal to plan and orchestrate

everything. Here the choice is: - IDE :: emacs because you focus on typing and don't get distracted by useless information - format :: .org files: they contain agenda, trees, graphs, attributes, source code... you can basically write a complete software within a file - LLM :: ollama because it's important to own the processes and limit spending - coding agent :: currently on [[https://pi.dev/][pi-agent]], [[https://opencode.ai/][opencode]] and [[https://aider.chat/][aider]] where not efficient with local models. * agent assistant

Agents can fulfill many tasks. The work has shifted from the paradigm of executing tasks (and often not document them) to document first what you want to do and plan (or let plan) the agents to execute.
The most important task is to test and quality check the results which means to own the pipeline and put enough logs and monitoring tools to allow traceability (know what agent did what).

We need an interface which is usually an IDE or a terminal to plan and orchestrate everything.

Here the choice is:

- IDE :: emacs because you focus on typing and don't get distracted by useless information
- format :: .org files: they contain agenda, trees, graphs, attributes, source code... you can basically write a complete software within a file
- LLM :: ollama because it's important to own the processes and limit spending
- coding agent :: currently on [[https://pi.dev/][pi-agent]], [[https://opencode.ai/][opencode]] and [[https://aider.chat/][aider]] where not efficient with local models. Aider UX is limited (no autocompletion, messed up my repo)
- MCP :: language models work at best with tools, I keep building MCP servers to ease LLM tasks
- graphs :: all the results are outputted in nodes and links to be visualized and navigated. I use [[https://neo4j.com/][neo4j]] to store the data
- programming :: mainly in python using REPL functionalities in emacs to test and execute every single line of code and check the data results
- deploy :: all the resources with docker so I can easily move them around
- hardware :: local: laptop and jetson

* models

Using mainly [[https://ollama.com/][ollama]] (with [[https://llama.app/][llama cpp]] took a lot of time for configuration) to serve LLMs.
Ollama has a nice interface for python which basically removed all my external dependencies from langchain and llamaindex (which keeps on changing APIs and packaging and my code needs to be re-written over and over).
I currently manage to run:
- `qwen2.5-coder:3b` :: I use it a lot for summarization tasks, it's quick but sometimes output trivial content
- `qwen3.5:9b` :: The least thinking model I can use
- `qwen3.6:latest` :: At the hardware limits of my local setup, it is not worth it the waiting, really few tokens per second
- `llama3.2:latest` ::

* coding assistant

The current coding assistant is on [[https://pi.dev/][pi-agent]] while [[https://opencode.ai/][opencode]], [[https://aider.chat/][aider]] and [[https://cursor.com/][cursor]] where also tested.
- pi-agent :: currently the running options because it's more efficient for local models. It reduces the load and unload of files and the number of tokens. 
- cursor ::  is not opensource and I can't integrated in my workflow. Cursor itself said that with using python REPL emacs it's the best option

* emacs

Emacs integrates bash commands with macros and program outputs, I can connect language models with mcp servers.
I currently use [[./emacs.el][emacs.el]] as current init file and [[./gptel_tools/el][gptel_tools.el]] for connecting with mcp. [[./gptell_allowed_commands.txt][gptel allowed commands]] is an additional list of bash commands which the tool allows
